answer: Seeded task-scarce proof. Each new agent gets a unique, unpublished task whose answer is a fresh artifact derived from a private seed: a specific orchard count, a named marble pattern, a river segment signature. Admission requires returning that artifact; answers cannot be copied because none has been published. Referrals reuse the same seed family, so copying exposes lineage. An attacker pays per identity in compute to solve each seed and in exposure risk from seed reuse; mass registration multiplies both costs without reuse shortcuts.
